newsitem.title: Turkey: FOCUS-Turkish investors wary of political worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Turkish investors wary of political worries.

text.p: Investors handed Turkey's creaking coalition government a resounding vote of no confidence on Friday, dumping shares and lira and sending domestic bond yields sharply higher.

A sharp sell-off sent the Istanbul Stock Exchange Index of 100 shares down as much as 5.7 percent. Prices later bounced back to end off 2.7 percent for the day, following a loss of 1.99 percent on Thursday.
Trade volume shrank to 17.16 trillion lira ($118.7 million) from Thursday's 20.91 trillion ($145.1 million), as players kept a wary eye on poltical developments.
"It was normal that reaction buys followed the extremely sharp falls earlier in the day. But caution remained ahead of the weekend," said Kadri Isik from Halk Securities.
"It may move either way depending on news to emerge from (the capital) Ankara."
Brokers said bearish sentiment was fuelled by disappointment that the Islamist-led coalition was still clinging to power despite almost daily defections that have cost it its parliamentary majority.
Investors are keen to see the year-old coalition, led by modern Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, give way to an alliance of secular parties, they said.
Instead, the government has vowed to stage early polls.
"The market had rallied in the past weeks on hopes that the coalition would collapse and a secularist alliance would be formed," said Hasan Soydan of Garanti Securities.

"But recent announcements show that there will be a change of the premiership between the coalition partners and the current government will move towards early elections. This news negatively affected the market," Soydan said.
The Turkish lira closed lower at 144,610 against the dollar from Thursday's 144,070 close, while bond yields rose around four percent.
The most active issue, April 22, 1998 paper, yielded 107.23 percent on Friday, up sharply from Thursday's 104.34.
"A private bank with a huge bond portfolio began to sell bonds late on Thursday on the over-the-counter (OTC) market, probably to close its short currency position," said one banker.

The sell-off in shares over the past two days marks an abrupt turnaround for a market that had appeared almost indifferent to the shifting fortunes of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his secular coalition partners.
The market index soared 4.6 percent last week and 8.7 percent the week before on widespread hopes than an alternative alliance would emerge to replace Erbakan and his Islam-based Welfare Party.

Bullish sentiment was reinforced by defections from the coalition, depriving it of a majority in the national assembly and clouding the prospects for an orderly handover of power from Erbakan to his deputy, secularist Tansu Ciller.
However, the government partners have remained adamant they would shore up its coalition and push the necessary legislation for an early election through parliament.
